messages:
Maria: Heads-up - we just saw 5 orgs get double-billed after a retry storm. Root cause looks like a race between reservation expiry and our dedupe window. Logs attached:

Maria: ```
2026-03-10T14:02:11Z INFO reserve created id=rcv_abc org=org_123 tokens=120 ttl=2s
2026-03-10T14:02:13Z WARN  request timeout id=req_456 -> client retried
2026-03-10T14:02:13Z INFO reserve expired id=rcv_abc
2026-03-10T14:02:13Z INFO charge committed id=chg_789 org=org_123 tokens=120
2026-03-10T14:02:13Z INFO charge committed id=chg_790 org=org_123 tokens=120
```

Alex: Ugh. Do we know if the retry had the same idempotency key?

Maria: In 3/5 cases the header was present but slightly different: trailing spaces or different case. One case missing header entirely (client lib bug).

Sam: That explains it. Our dedupe uses exact idempotency-key + org + endpoint. We need stronger canonicalization and a fallback fingerprint when header absent.

Lina: Also the reserve TTL (2s) < dedupe window (5s) so a retry arriving after reserve expiry will still get charged if dedupe fails. Race between reserve lifecycle and dedupe correctness.

Alex: Proposal: 1) canonicalize idempotency key (trim, collapse whitespace, lowercase) on ingest 2) support computed fingerprint header: X-Request-Fingerprint = sha256(method + path + body) 3) extend reserve TTL to 6s or make reserve tied to dedupe token lifecycle 4) produce metric quota.charge.double_count when we see two charges for same dedupe id within 10s

Maria: +1. For (3) I prefer tying reserve->dedupe token so reserve doesn't expire before dedupe window. That avoids having to increase all TTLs arbitrarily.

Sam: Implementation note: storing dedupe tokens in the same transactional ledger that commits charges avoids a window where reserve expires but commit still runs. We can 1) create reserve record with dedupe_id 2) when commit scans, consult reserve record -> atomically mark charged. If reserve deleted due to TTL, treat commit as stale and consult dedupe index lookup by fingerprint before charging.

Alex: Pseudocode for canonicalization check we can put in edge-proxy: ```
function normalizeIdemp(k){ return k ? k.trim().replace(/\s+/g,' ').toLowerCase() : null }
// if null compute fingerprint and set X-Request-Fingerprint
```

Lina: We also need better telemetry on the console: expose a per-org "pending reservations" gauge, and a per-key "last_charge_ts" in the quota debug view. Devs kept saying they couldn't tell why things looked charged twice.

quota-bot: Alert created: INCIDENT-2026-0310-dupcharge (severity: minor). Links: https://incidents.internal/2026-0310-dupcharge

Maria: Rollout plan: make canonicalization + fingerprint read-only on canary for 48h (log mismatches), then enable dedupe lookup using both canonical idemp and fingerprint for 7 days, then switch to normalize-only. Why: avoid breaking clients that intentionally vary keys.

Alex: We'll need an API compat header so client libs can opt-in earlier: X-Quota-Dedupe-Mode: legacy|compat|strict. Default legacy for now. Add warning header when legacy used and mismatch detected.

Sam: Tests: unit for normalizeIdemp, integration that simulates 504+retry path, e2e with chaos (delayed reserve expiry). Add a regression test asserting quota.charge.double_count==0 for the scenario.

Lina: Ops: create runbook step to temporarily increase reserve TTL to 10s for hotfix if we see >10 dup charges in an hour. Also add alert when quota.charge.double_count > 3 in 1m for any org.

Maria: Who owns the change? Alex + Sam to pair on server + proxy changes. Lina to add alerts and console fields. I'll send the PR template and mark as high-priority for next sprint.

Alex: Ack. I'll open the PR with feature-flag guard (flag=dedupe_canonicalization) and add migration notes.

Sam: Adding an integration harness entry: `tests/duplicates/retry_race_test.py` that exercises reserve TTL boundary.

Maria: Cool. Let's reconvene after the canary run. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
